Hi David,

Thanks again for the product tour yesterday. We ran a quick sizing pass with our infra team and have a few concrete questions while we prep an internal business case:

- Can you summarize how retention buckets are priced (hot/nearline/archive) and whether there are breakpoints for ingested spans above 1B/day?
- For distributed tracing: does the tracing add-on include sampling-based credits, and can we get a short-term sampling exception during the pilot?
- Advanced dashboards: we need an estimate for seat vs. seatless dashboard pricing for up to 15 power users and 150 active non-power users.

We’re also exploring a 90-day pilot tied to a small SOW. What flexibility do you have on pilot credits (ingest + retention) and a demo-level dashboard credit so the execs can evaluate value quickly?

Attached: our internal telemetry growth forecast (attachment stub: brightline_forecast_q4.csv).

Subject: Re: Observability add-ons: retention, tracing & advanced dashboards — packaging and pilot credits

Hi Anna — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers and proposed next steps below.

Retention pricing: we have three canonical tiers (hot / warm / archive). Pricing breaks at ingestion thresholds (monthly tokens/spans). At ~1B spans/day we recommend a hybrid hot+nearline mix to keep per-token cost reasonable; we can model exact numbers against your forecast.

Tracing: the tracing add-on includes flexible sampling and a pilot-friendly exception. For pilots we commonly provide an elevated sampling allowance (covers bursty debugging traffic) plus a short-term sampling override for 90 days.

Dashboards: seat vs seatless — for 15 power users we usually recommend 12 seats + 40 seatless viewers for dashboards; we will provide both a seat-based and a seatless+ingest estimate so you can compare.

Pilot credits: we can offer a 90-day pilot with the following starting point: 60% off retention charges (up to a capped amount), 100k span ingest credits, and a one-time demo dashboard credit to populate up to 5 dashboards. This is provisional — Ben and I want to run the financials and confirm the capped amounts.

Next steps:
- Can we schedule a 45-minute pricing workshop Monday to run the forecast through our pricing model?
- I’ll loop in Ben and Irene to finalize a formal SOW + credit schedule.

I’ve attached a short checklist we use for pilots (attachment stub: pilot_checklist.txt).

Best,
David Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
david_kim@redwood.com

Subject: Fwd: Observability add-ons: pilot credits — Brightline (prep + ask)

Ben / Irene — forwarding Anna’s list with my notes. High level: Brightline is a mid-stage health tech customer (HLT-4821) evaluating ops observability for an expand from logging-only -> traces + dashboards. Their forecast shows an expected jump to ~1.2B spans/day during peak windows. They want a 90-day pilot + executive dashboard credits.

Key ask: what’s our concession envelope for a pilot that meaningfully proves value without locking our economics? My initial proposal:
- Pilot length: 90 days
- Retention credits: cover 60% of archive/warm retention costs up to $18k total (customer pays overage if they exceed)
- Ingest credits: 100k span-equivalent credits included
- Dashboard: one demo credit for 5 dashboards + data connectors (one-time)
- Volume discount: reserve option to offer year-1 25% discount on add-ons if they commit to Dedicated capacity within 90 days (we need legal/finance to ok)

Irene — can you run an earnback-style model with capped exposure (max $18k) and confirm we’re comfortable with the technical scope for the demo credit? Ben — if we can do the 25% commit discount, can you take point on the commercial terms?

Quoted below is Anna’s original email for context.
